context: Each edit can insert (add), delete, or replace one character.
description: The two panels align characters by position. From top to bottom, each shows the source string, an intermediate row showing the edits, and the target string. Arrows identify the type of edit and the corresponding character positions. They do not prescribe a unique order for the three edits.

The left panel converts s = kitten to t = sitting. Replace the first letter k with s (blue), replace the fifth letter e with i (blue), and append g (purple). The other 4 letters, i, t, t, and n, stay the same. Vertical dashed lines align the intermediate and target rows. The intermediate row reads s, i, t, t, i, n, g, with the replacement letters s and i in blue and the new g in purple. Its characters already match the target. The length grows from 6 characters to 7.

The right panel converts s = hello to t = algo. Delete the initial h, which appears faded in pale orange in the intermediate row and does not carry through to the target. Replace the second letter e with a (blue) and the second of the two consecutive l characters with g (blue). The first l and the final o stay the same. Vertical dashed lines align the intermediate and target rows. The intermediate row shows the faded h followed by a, l, g, o. The target row contains only a, l, g, o. The length drops from 5 characters to 4.

frames.explanation: The figure does not label the total step count. The table gives 3 for each example because two replacements plus one insertion or deletion make three edits, matching the minimum given in the text.
frames.title: Character alignments for two three-step edits

summary: Side-by-side character alignments show how to convert kitten to sitting and hello to algo. Both conversions require a minimum of 3 edits.
title: Edit distance: two three-step conversions
